topics.title: Atomic masses and composition of the nucleus

concepts.learning_objective: Define the atomic mass unit and calculate the average atomic mass of an element from its isotopic abundances.
Describe the nucleus in terms of Z, N and A and explain how the neutron was discovered.
Classify nuclides as isotopes, isobars or isotones from their Z, N and A.
Use R = R0 A^(1/3) to find and compare nuclear radii.
Explain why nuclear density is independent of mass number and compare it with ordinary matter.
Apply E = mc^2 and the relation 1 u = 931.5 MeV/c^2.
Calculate mass defect, binding energy and binding energy per nucleon of a nucleus.
Interpret the binding energy per nucleon curve to compare the stability of nuclei.
State the properties of the nuclear force: strong, short-ranged and charge independent.
Interpret the potential energy curve of a pair of nucleons as a function of separation.
Recall Becquerel's discovery of radioactivity and that it is a nuclear phenomenon.
Identify alpha, beta and gamma decay and the changes they produce in a nucleus.
Compare the energy released in nuclear and chemical processes and explain mass-energy interconversion in both.
Balance fission reactions and estimate the energy released in fission.

topics.title: Nuclear fusion in stars and controlled fusion

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why fusion needs very high temperatures to overcome the Coulomb barrier.
Describe the proton-proton cycle by which hydrogen fuses into helium in the sun.
State the main challenge of controlled thermonuclear fusion in a reactor.
